action_summary: Compose the existing counted test runner with the live cross-file repair path and adapt existing report relocation and execution-state guards. No pinned adapter is changed. Producer-run tests are development evidence; independent verification is pending. Extend the same no-retry-after-effects rule to the local DAG-to-kernel fallback. Add a local, pre-test refusal for the pinned test-adequacy adapter when more than one target file would be collapsed into line-number-only evidence; preserve the adapter and single-file path. Compose a local context-sensitive refusal around the pinned taint adapter so its cross-context sanitizer false negatives are not published.
causal_blocker: Unverified repair evidence, context-insensitive sanitizers, cross-file line identity loss, and unsafe path or retry binding can report success or repeat effects without validating the intended task.
expected_parent_frontier_change: Refuse live cross-file repair success without a counted passing test suite, and reduce unintended report writes and duplicate action dispatch. Independent qualification pending. Locally reject the demonstrated multi-file adequacy false-positive without re-running the test suite or changing pinned bytes. Withhold a local negative taint result when a contextual sanitizer may have hidden a sink flow; retain the pinned adapter and its positive findings.

route_order_assessment.DELETE: Deleting repair, output, or testing loses useful engineering capability.
route_order_assessment.BYPASS: Bypassing the repair adapter does not preserve the existing repair route.
route_order_assessment.REUSE: Reuse the existing suite_argv runner and the adapter workspace resolver; the repair adapter does not use the stronger runner. Reuse the adequacy adapter path resolver and its target-selection semantics for a narrow preflight. Reuse the taint adapter parser, sink vocabulary, and report; the existing Bandit diff gate requires a diff and does not implement this source-to-sink contract.
route_order_assessment.ADAPT: The earlier path and execution-state guards are adapted at the live seam.
route_order_assessment.SUBSTITUTE: Substituting a different repair engine would change task coverage and requires separate qualification.
route_order_assessment.COMPOSE: Combine the pinned adapter with the existing test runner, withholding its report until the fresh suite passes. Compose a conservative multi-file admission guard ahead of the adequacy adapter; the existing diff-coverage tool has a different input and effect contract. Stage the actual pinned taint report and admit a negative result only when the narrow sanitizer hazard is absent.

independent_oracle: On fresh disposable projects, observe test-process results, actual source bytes, and the requested report, then seek an independently executed run; none has yet occurred.
blocker_lease_key: 2026-10-09-resource-bounded-bytes-v1::GENERAL_REUSABLE_PROBLEM_SOLVING_CAPABILITY_FRONTIER::Unverified repair evidence, context-insensitive sanitizers, cross-file line identity loss, and unsafe path or retry binding can report success or repeat effects without validating the intended task.
measured_effect: Producer-run focused suite: 24 passed, including fresh false-verification, report-alias, real surviving repair side effect, and single/DAG retry controls. Four of five initial verifier tests failed before the wrapper; the real DAG fallback wrote twice before the fix. Broader suites: 55 passed, 18 failed (13 goal-front and 5 typed/effect failures match previously observed baselines). A five-sample tiny warm-project timing gave median 48.6 ms pinned direct versus 118.2 ms live guarded; this is not an equivalent end-to-end benchmark or a speed gain. No independent verifier, full-suite result, or capability-credit claim. Added a local preflight for the proven cross-file adequacy bug: 2 of 3 initial tests failed before the guard, including the live route falsely reporting success, and the single-file control passed. The expanded producer-run focused suites passed 46 tests, including the existing direct-adapter controls. One tiny single-file, eight-sample timing showed median 43.96 ms direct pinned versus 48.75 ms local guarded; this is not an equivalent end-to-end benchmark or a speed gain. Added a narrow staged local taint guard: 6 of 8 initial tests failed before the guard, including an actual html.escape/exec false negative and report hardlink overwrite; 13 extended taint tests pass. The combined producer-run selected suites pass 59 tests. A 40-sample tiny fixture measured median 0.490 ms direct pinned vs 1.806 ms local guarded; these are not equivalent end-to-end paths or a speed gain. Before PR preparation, the selected 59-test suite was rerun by the producer and passed; this is not independent verification.
known_limitations: The wrapper is limited to the live local cross-file adapter route; direct or other controller paths remain outside its scope.
Verification executes project code and is not a sandbox; timeouts, non-file effects and concurrent modifications remain risks.
The wrapper does not roll back changes when post-repair checks fail; failures are marked as having possible effects and no verified report is published.
The no-duplicate change does not ensure exactly-once execution across crashes or external retries.
Load-bearing primary admission and independent verification remain incomplete.
Local DAG fallback must conservatively treat loaded adapters and unexpected exceptions as potentially side-effecting; this is not durable exactly-once execution.

The producer-side runner adaptation refuses script-only oracles, even valid ones, and incurs extra test-process overhead; this is a deliberate fail-closed tradeoff, not evidence of no capability regression.
A pre-existing report at the requested destination is not removed on failure; consumers must respect the returned failure and cannot treat an old artifact as the current result.
The completion marker is not an adversarially trusted channel; project code runs with the process privileges and can interfere with the checker.
The multi-file adequacy guard is a refusal, not a file-aware coverage implementation; direct calls and non-local execution paths remain unaffected.
The single-file adequacy adapter still cannot prove test adequacy, and its negative-proof scope and suite validity require further work.
The adequacy guard intentionally refuses valid multi-file requests; no file-aware replacement is registered or claimed as independently verified.
The adequacy preflight is not a filesystem lock: concurrent file changes can invalidate its subject count.
The pinned single-file adequacy adapter can still report success with an empty or skipped suite and overstates what an unexecuted line proves; the guard only addresses file-identity loss.
Taint context guard is a conservative local post-check for quote/escape false negatives, not a context-aware taint engine; non-local paths and other false negatives are unaffected.
A negative taint result still means no path the analyzer could see, not proof of safety. The guard may refuse safe code and is subject to concurrent changes.
The taint guard can refuse harmless code when quote/escape and a sink are unrelated; it does not validate every sanitization function or detect all existing taint false negatives.
The guard is scoped to the local live entry and is not a security sandbox, independent verifier, or proof that a negative answer means safe.
Successful staged taint reports replace the destination atomically, which changes its inode and can change existing metadata such as permissions or extended attributes.
The local taint route still returns no for a demonstrated source-to-sink flow passed through another function argument; executing the fixture printed 456.
A user-defined method named int can be mistaken for numeric sanitization: the local taint route returned no while a fixture executed untrusted code.
